text: When you work with APIs, you typically send HTTP requests to a server to get or send data. Most modern APIs use JSON, a simple text format that both humans and computers can read easily. Before making any request, you often need authentication, such as an API key or a token, to prove who you are. Another important thing to know is rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a certain time period. If you exceed them, the server may block you temporarily. Finally, always include error handling in your code. This means checking the response status and dealing with problems gracefully, so your program doesn’t crash when something goes wrong.
